pharm: Parenteral first-generation cephalosporin; time-dependent bactericidal beta-lactam with activity against gram-positive cocci (incl. MSSA) and some gram-negative bacilli.
quick: 500 mg-1 g IV/IM q6-8h (up to 1-1.5 g q6h severe)
Generally considered acceptable; cephalosporins widely used
No disulfiram-like reaction (no MTT side chain)
summary: Cefazolin is a parenteral first-generation cephalosporin, the standard agent for surgical antibiotic prophylaxis and for serious infections caused by MSSA and susceptible streptococci. Given IV or IM, it requires renal dose adjustment. It does not cover MRSA, enterococci, or most resistant gram-negatives, and is contraindicated in patients with cephalosporin allergy.
indications: Respiratory tract infections (S. pneumoniae, Klebsiella, H. influenzae, S. aureus, group A strep)
Urinary tract infections (E. coli, P. mirabilis, Klebsiella, some enterobacter/enterococci)
Skin and skin structure infections (S. aureus, streptococci)
Septicemia and endocarditis due to susceptible organisms

dosage.t: 0.5-1 h before incision; 500 mg-1 g intraop if >=2 h; 500 mg-1 g q6-8h for 24 h post-op
dosage.n: Re-dose intraoperatively for long procedures/major blood loss

admin: Reconstitute and give by direct IV injection over 3-5 minutes, by IV infusion, or by deep IM injection into a large muscle
For surgical prophylaxis, administer 0.5-1 hour before incision
Adjust dose interval in renal impairment
Inspect reconstituted solution for particulate matter
moa: Binds penicillin-binding proteins and inhibits the final transpeptidation step of bacterial cell wall peptidoglycan synthesis, leading to cell lysis; time-dependent bactericidal activity.

absolute: Known allergy to the cephalosporin group of antibiotics

preg: Cephalosporins are widely used and generally considered acceptable in pregnancy when indicated.
lact: Excreted in breast milk in low concentrations; considered compatible with breastfeeding with monitoring of the infant.
renal: Requires dose reduction and/or interval extension based on creatinine clearance; primarily renally eliminated.

moderate: Probenecid - decreases renal tubular secretion, increases and prolongs cefazolin levels
Concurrent nephrotoxic agents (aminoglycosides) - potential additive nephrotoxicity
interactions.alcohol: No disulfiram-like reaction (cefazolin lacks an N-methylthiotetrazole side chain).
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-positive urine glucose with copper-reduction (Clinitest) tests and positive direct Coombs test.

monitoring: Renal function in prolonged therapy or impairment
Diarrhea/possible C. difficile during or after therapy
counsel: Report rash, hives, swelling, or difficulty breathing immediately
Report severe or persistent diarrhea (may occur even weeks after treatment)
Tell your clinician about any penicillin or cephalosporin allergy
This medicine is given by injection in hospital/clinic
pk: IM ~1-2 h; IV at end of infusion
~1.8 h (normal renal function); prolonged in renal impairment
Store powder per label; reconstituted solution per stability instructions
pearls: Drug of choice for MSSA infections and the standard surgical prophylaxis agent
Does NOT cover MRSA, enterococci, or most resistant gram-negative bacilli
Lacks N-methylthiotetrazole side chain - no disulfiram-like reaction or hypoprothrombinemia like some other cephalosporins
Poor CNS penetration - not for meningitis
Often preferred over cefuroxime for prophylaxis due to long history and cost
missed: Hospital/clinic-administered. If a dose is delayed, give as soon as possible and adjust subsequent timing; do not double up.
overdose: May cause neurotoxicity (seizures), especially in renal impairment. Provide supportive care; hemodialysis can remove cefazolin.
